title: Exact residue reduction on the triangulated category of complete integral complexes
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme on its fixed small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\ell$ be prime and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\pi_E$ and finite residue field $\kappa=\mathcal O_E/\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $R_X=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ and $S_X=p_X^*\underline\kappa$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and use ordinary unbounded module derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Write $C(K)$ for derived $\pi_E$-completeness, namely invertibility of the specified canonical map $K\to R\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(K\otimes^L_{R_X}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X)$ [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]. Then $C(0)$ holds, $C$ is invariant under isomorphisms, $C(K[r])\Longleftrightarrow C(K)$ for every integer $r$, and in every ambient distinguished triangle any two complete vertices imply completeness of the third. Let $\kappa_X^{\mathrm{cst}}$ be the sheafification of the constant ring presheaf, and let $\kappa_X^{\mathrm{cont}}=(U\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|U|),\kappa))^\#$ with the quotient topology on $\pi_0(|U|)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The constant-function morphism $\kappa_X^{\mathrm{cst}}\to\kappa_X^{\mathrm{cont}}$ is a ring-sheaf isomorphism. Together with the finite discrete coefficient comparison [lem-sf-module-object-ordinary-coefficient-equivalence], it identifies $S_X$ with this same constant coefficient ring, by isomorphisms agreeing on every constant scalar. Under this identification, derived extension of scalars along $R_X\to S_X$, retaining the $S_X$-module structure [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], gives an exact functor $T_1:D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_X))\to D(\operatorname{Mod}(\kappa_X^{\mathrm{cont}}))$, whose value is the actual residue reduction $K\otimes^L_{R_X}S_X$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. This functor preserves zero, isomorphisms, all integer shifts and distinguished triangles, and its restriction to the strictly full subcategory of complete objects is triangulated. Neither boundedness of the integral complexes nor any Noetherian, quasi-compactness, dimension, finite-type or invertibility hypothesis on $X$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pe-completion-triangle-comparison] in the specified coefficient category: it supplies an additive endofunctor $F$, a natural transformation $c:\mathrm{id}\Rightarrow F$, and $C(K)\Longleftrightarrow c_K$ invertible for the actual canonical completion map. Since $F$ is additive, $F(0)$ is zero (its identity is $F(0)=0$), so $c_0$ is invertible. For an isomorphism $e:K\to L$, naturality gives $c_L=F(e)c_Ke^{-1}$, proving isomorphism invariance. Its shift equation $\sigma_{K,r}c_{K[r]}=c_K[r]$, with $\sigma_{K,r}$ invertible and $[r]$ an equivalence, proves $C(K[r])\Longleftrightarrow C(K)$.

source.place: Cones paragraph: canonical completion maps and shifts

proof.text: For a distinguished triangle $T=(K\to L\to M\to K[1])$, [lem-pe-completion-triangle-comparison] supplies a distinguished image triangle $F(T)$ and the morphism $(c_K,c_L,c_M)$, including the square with $c_K[1]$. If any two vertices are complete, the corresponding two components are invertible. Apply [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] to obtain invertibility of the third, and hence its completeness. Together with step 1 these are the hypotheses of [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]; the strictly full complete subcategory therefore has the inherited triangulation and exact inclusion.

For every site object $U$, a continuous map $|U|\to\kappa$ is constant on every connected component, because $\kappa$ is discrete. Its induced function on $\pi_0(|U|)$ is continuous by the definition of the quotient topology; conversely composition with the quotient is continuous. These mutually inverse operations commute with restriction and pointwise ring operations. Thus the presheaf in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] is the continuous-function ring presheaf on $|U|$. The discrete-target clause of [lem-sfb-continuous-set-descent-components] says this presheaf is already a sheaf and identifies the constant set sheaf with it by constant functions. By [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets], the underlying set maps of the ring sheafifications defining $\kappa_X^{\mathrm{cst}}$ and $\kappa_X^{\mathrm{cont}}$ are the set sheafifications; so $\kappa_X^{\mathrm{cont}}$ is this sheaf and $a$ is that bijection. As $a$ preserves $0,1,+,\cdot$, it is an isomorphism of ring sheaves. This proves that the specified constant-function map $a:\kappa_X^{\mathrm{cst}}\to\kappa_X^{\mathrm{cont}}$ is invertible, without a quasi-compactness assumption.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-module-object-ordinary-coefficient-equivalence] to the finite commutative discrete ring $\kappa$ and the same scheme $X$. Choose its coefficient isomorphism in the normalized form provided by [lem-sf-finite-discrete-normalized-encoding]: $b:\kappa_X^{\mathrm{cst}}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_X$ sends each constant scalar to that scalar in the pulled-back ring. Set $e=a b^{-1}:S_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa_X^{\mathrm{cont}}$. For a constant scalar $u$, $e(b(u))=a(u)$ is the constant function $u$. Hence the two identifications agree on every constant scalar. By the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], ring maps from the associated constant ring sheaf with these scalar values are equal; the identification is the specified one.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] to the actual ring-sheaf map $R_X\to S_X$. It gives the everywhere-defined exact functor $F_1=-\otimes^L_{R_X}S_X$ with values in $D(S_X)$, retaining its $S_X$-action. To compare with the relative tensor convention [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], take a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The section-action equivalence of [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] identifies the relative tensor complex with the ordinary sheaf tensor complex by $p\otimes s\mapsto p\otimes s$, and preserves and reflects K-flatness. Its acyclic-test K-flat representatives also preserve quasi-isomorphisms: tensoring $\operatorname{Cone}(u)$ gives $\operatorname{Cone}(P\otimes u)$, which is acyclic. Thus both derived constructions are computed by $P\otimes_{R_X}S_X$ and give the actual residue reduction with its $S_X$-module structure, naturally in $K$.

proof.text: Relabel an $S_X$-module by letting $t\in\kappa_X^{\mathrm{cont}}$ act as $e^{-1}(t)$. This is an additive equivalence with inverse relabelling through $e$; it leaves the underlying abelian sheaves and maps unchanged, so kernels and cokernels are unchanged and it is exact. By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] its termwise derived functor $D(e_*)$ commutes with shifts and preserves distinguished triangles. Set $T_1=D(e_*)F_1$. Both factors are exact; consequently $T_1$ preserves zero, all shifts and distinguished triangles, and, as a functor, preserves isomorphisms. On a K-flat representative its value is precisely $P\otimes_{R_X}S_X$ with the coefficient relabelling of step 4. Compose with the exact inclusion from step 2 to obtain its triangulated restriction to complete objects. All cited completion and coefficient results apply to arbitrary $X$ and unbounded complexes; no geometric finiteness or invertibility condition has entered.
